slides.headline: Before we code: mobile basics
items: Expo vs React Native (what they are)
How a mobile app runs (lifecycle)
Expo Go setup (fastest path today)
Hybrid vs native (what it means)
Why we avoid Swift/Kotlin at first

slides.headline: What is React Native?
items: Build iOS + Android apps with JavaScript/TypeScript + React
UI is native components (not a web page)
Runs JS in a JS engine (Hermes/JavaScriptCore)
Uses native modules for device features (camera, maps, etc.)
Metro bundles code and enables fast reload in dev
slides.footnote: React Native uses different components than React for web.

slides.headline: What is Expo?
slides.body: Expo is a toolkit and SDK on top of React Native that helps you start fast, test on a real phone, and use common device features without heavy native setup.
items: Create apps with create-expo-app
Expo Go: run projects on your phone quickly
Expo SDK: camera, notifications, location, etc.
EAS: build and ship to the app stores
Add native code later if you need it

left.title: React Native
items: Framework for native iOS/Android UI
JS/TS code + React components
Native modules for platform features
Needs native tools to build binaries

right.title: Expo
items: CLI, SDK, and good defaults
Expo Go for quick device testing
EAS Build/Update for shipping
Config plugins for native setup

slides.headline: App types (web, native, hybrid)

cards.title: Web app
cards.subtitle: Runs in a browser
cards.description: One codebase, easiest to share, but limited access to device features.

cards.title: Native app
cards.subtitle: Swift / Kotlin
cards.description: Best platform access and performance, but you maintain iOS and Android separately.

cards.title: Hybrid (React Native)
cards.subtitle: One app, two platforms
cards.description: Single UI codebase that renders native components on both iOS and Android.

slides.footnote: React Native is “hybrid” in codebase, but the UI is native.

slides.headline: Why not Swift/Kotlin first?
items: Two codebases (iOS + Android) doubles effort
Harder setup (Xcode/Android Studio on day 1)
Slower iteration for UI changes
Expo/RN keeps focus on one language (JS/TS)
You can still go native later when needed

slides.headline: Mobile app lifecycle (simplified)
items: Install → open the app
Launch → app starts and loads the JS bundle
Foreground → user interacts
Background → user switches apps (pause some work)
Terminated → OS closes the app; next open is a fresh launch

left.title: iOS
items: Install Expo Go from the App Store
Open it and allow camera access
Run npx expo start on your computer
Scan the QR code with Expo Go

right.title: Android
items: Install Expo Go from Google Play
Open it and allow camera permissions
Run npx expo start on your computer
Scan the QR code inside Expo Go

slides.headline: If Expo Go won’t connect (quick fixes)
items: Phone + computer on the same Wi‑Fi network
Disable VPN/firewall, or use tunnel mode
Try: npx expo start --tunnel
Confirm Metro is running and QR is current
If scanning fails, paste the link manually
slides.footnote: Rule of thumb: get Expo Go working first, then simulators.

slides.headline: Prompt: Check Expo readiness
slides.title: Copy into Cursor Chat (run commands, verify each step).
slides.prompt:
Help me set up my computer for Expo (React Native) development using Cursor.

Goals:
- I want to run an Expo app on my real phone with Expo Go.
- I also want to run it on iOS Simulator and Android Emulator if possible.

Please:
1) Check my OS and Node.js version.
2) Verify I can run npx and install packages.
3) Check if Expo tooling is available (and install the recommended way if not).
4) If I’m on macOS, check for Xcode and iOS Simulator availability.
5) Check for Android Studio / Android SDK / emulator availability.
6) Summarize what’s missing and the fastest path to get running today.

Keep it concise. Run commands and explain results.
slides.footnote: Goal: get Expo Go working first, then simulators.

slides.headline: Prompt: Create the Expo app
slides.title: Expo Router + TypeScript + a clean project baseline.
slides.prompt:
Create a new Expo app for me with these constraints:
- Use TypeScript
- Use Expo Router for navigation (file-based routes)
- Project name: ufg-places

Steps:
1) Pick the correct create-expo-app command for the current Expo version.
2) Create the project and install dependencies.
3) Explain where the routes live and what file is the entry point.
4) Start the dev server and tell me how to open it in Expo Go.

If anything fails, diagnose and fix the root cause (don’t handwave). Keep explanations short.
slides.footnote: Keep the scope tight: one screen first, then iterate.

slides.headline: Expo Router entry points
items: Root layout: app/_layout.tsx (wraps all routes)
Initial route: first matching index.tsx for /
Route groups: app/(tabs)/... (group not in URL)
Dynamic routes: app/places/[id].tsx
Keep routes small: UI + data + navigation
slides.footnote: If you’re lost: start at app/_layout.tsx, then app/index.tsx.

slides.headline: Prompt: Add NativeWind
slides.title: Install and verify styling works on device.
slides.prompt:
I have an Expo Router + TypeScript app named "ufg-places".

Help me add NativeWind with the simplest working setup.

Requirements:
- Configure Tailwind + NativeWind so I can use className on React Native components.
- Add a tiny demo on app/index.tsx:
  - A screen with a title, a subtitle, and a primary button
  - Use safe area
  - Make it look clean and readable

After setup:
1) Tell me how to verify styles are applied in Expo Go.
2) If styles don’t apply, diagnose the root cause and fix it.

Keep explanations short and command-driven.
slides.footnote: Target: consistent spacing, readable typography, safe area.

slides.headline: Prompt: Set up Supabase data
slides.title: Create project, tables, seed, and safe RLS defaults.
slides.prompt:
I’m building a mobile app called "UFG Places" with Expo + Supabase.

Help me do the Supabase setup end-to-end:

1) Create a new Supabase project and give it a clear name.
2) Create these tables: categories, places, favorites.
3) Seed categories and at least 10 example places.
4) Enable Row Level Security (RLS).
5) Add simple policies:
   - Anyone can read categories + places.
   - Only signed-in users can insert/delete their own favorites.

Then:
- Tell me how to verify the data with 2-3 SQL queries.
- Give me a checklist of what values I need in my Expo env config (URL + anon key).

Keep it practical: minimal schema, minimal policies, real data.
slides.footnote: We’ll keep places public, favorites private.

slides.headline: Prompt: GitHub login (Supabase)
slides.title: Enable GitHub OAuth and wire it into Expo.
slides.prompt:
I need GitHub OAuth sign-in in an Expo app using Supabase Auth.

Context:
- Project: Expo Router + TypeScript
- Backend: Supabase
- Auth provider: GitHub
- Target: Works in Expo Go + a development build

Please:
1) In Supabase, enable the GitHub provider and explain what callback/redirect URLs I must configure for Expo.
2) In my Expo app, add Supabase client setup using env vars.
3) Implement:
   - Sign in with GitHub button
   - Handle redirect back to the app
   - Persist session and show signed-in state
   - Sign out
4) Keep the UI minimal and clear (NativeWind).
5) If there are platform-specific issues (Expo Go vs dev build), explain the smallest workable path for today.

Be explicit and step-by-step. Include quick verification steps after each major change.
slides.footnote: Goal: you can sign in, see your profile state, and sign out.

slides.headline: Prompt: Build the screens
slides.title: Routes, queries, and a shippable UX.
slides.prompt:
Help me implement the core screens for "UFG Places" using Expo Router + TypeScript.

Routes:
- app/(tabs)/_layout.tsx: tabs for Home, Favorites, Profile
- app/(tabs)/index.tsx: places list
- app/places/[id].tsx: place detail
- app/(tabs)/favorites.tsx: my favorites list
- app/(tabs)/profile.tsx: auth state + sign in/out

Data:
- Fetch places + categories from Supabase.
- Favorites should be per-user (requires auth).

UX requirements:
- Search on the places list
- Filter by category
- Tap a place to open details
- Favorite/unfavorite from list and detail
- Show loading + error states (simple)

Keep components small, prioritize readability, and tell me how to test each screen quickly in Expo Go.
slides.footnote: Scope: ship the core flow before polishing.

slides.headline: Prompt: Debug Expo/Supabase issues
slides.title: Use this any time you get stuck (paste logs verbatim).
slides.prompt:
I’m building an Expo app with Supabase and I’m stuck.

Here’s what I expected:
[describe expected behavior]

Here’s what happened:
[describe actual behavior]

Here are the logs (Metro, device, emulator, Supabase errors):
[paste logs verbatim]

Please:
1) Generate 3-5 likely root causes (ranked).
2) For the top cause, give me exact steps to verify it.
3) Then give me the smallest fix.
4) Tell me how to confirm the fix worked on both Expo Go and a simulator.

Keep it practical and short.
slides.footnote: Rule: don’t summarize errors—paste them exactly.
